extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A public multimodal dataset pairing 50,188 reconstructed non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes from 25,692 scans of 21,304 unique patients with corresponding radiology reports. It includes anonymized acquisition metadata, report-derived labels for 18 abnormalities, organ-level anatomical segmentation labels, and a derived visual question-answering dataset containing over 2.7 million question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci
extraction.citeAs: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci. CT-RATE: Paired chest CT volumes and radiology reports. https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE. 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology reports were curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. Every reconstructed volume from the hospital database was incorporated to capture different reconstruction techniques, followed by quality control excluding contrast-enhanced volumes and body regions other than the chest. The cohort contains 21,304 unique patients, with 20,000 allocated to training and 1,304 to validation. Ethical approval for open-sourcing the dataset and associated models was granted by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee at Istanbul Medipol University on 27 October 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Hospital database records from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital: non-contrast chest CT volumes, acquisition metadata, and corresponding radiologist-authored reports structured into clinical information, technique, findings, and impression sections. The original reports were in Turkish. The released dataset contains original raw imaging data and English versions of the anonymized reports.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized using regular-expression searches to remove date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. They were translated from Turkish into English using the Google Translate API, then reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students, who also removed residual personal information and checked coherence. Identifying information about patients and medical professionals was removed from CT metadata. Only English report versions are released.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Contrast-enhanced volumes and volumes involving body parts other than the chest were excluded. Volume orientation was standardized using metadata. For model processing, volumes were resized to uniform spacing of 0.75 mm along the x and y axes and 1.5 mm along the z axis, then center-cropped or padded to 480 × 480 × 240 voxels. Values were converted to Hounsfield Units using metadata intercept and slope, clipped to -1000 to 1000, and normalized to -1 to 1 during training. Preprocessing scripts are provided in the GitHub repository. Derived VQA data were selected for accuracy and proper formatting, including successful JSON parsing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Radiologists authored the original reports. For abnormality labeling, 1,000 reports were manually annotated after combining findings and impression sections, producing multi-label annotations for 18 abnormalities. Conditions not mentioned in either section were considered absent. Similar descriptions were grouped, including lung opacity, density increase, and ground-glass opacities under lung opacity, and lung and fissural nodules under lung nodules. The annotated reports were split into 800 training and 200 validation reports to fine-tune RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, which classified the remaining 24,692 reports. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model. For the derived VQA dataset, Llama 3.1 8B generated long-answer and multiple-choice questions from reports and text-only questions from 48,343 chest-CT-related PubMed Central open-access articles. Short-answer questions were generated using a rule-based approach, and report-generation questions were sampled from predefined prompts and paired with corresponding reports.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Findings and impression sections were combined because some abnormalities were not explicitly mentioned in a single section. Unmentioned conditions were treated as absent, and related descriptions were consolidated into common labels. The automated report labeler was evaluated on the 200-report validation split using per-abnormality precision, recall, and F1 scores; reported F1 scores ranged from 0.95 to 1.00. Generated VQA examples were selected for accuracy and proper formatting.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Original reports were authored by numerous radiologists. Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected report translations and checked for residual personal information.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m fine-tuned report labeler; Llama 3.1 8B for VQA generation; rule-based short-answer generation; CADS anatomical segmentation model; TotalSegmentator for pulmonary-nodule masks and derived structured nodule information.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels as future work. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are already available through the Hugging Face repository. No update schedule, dataset versioning policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age and sex are included in released metadata. Ages range from 18 to 102 years, with a mean of 48.8 years; the reported sex distribution is 41.6% female and 58.4% male. The source reports include patient symptoms, medical history, anatomical findings, abnormalities, and diagnoses. Data originate from a hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. All CT volumes, associated metadata, and reports were anonymized before computational analysis, with identifying information about patients and medical professionals removed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The open release is intended to address the scarcity of paired 3D medical images and reports, support medical AI research, and provide a foundation for future clinically deployable systems. Potential benefits discussed include reducing radiologists' workloads, improving diagnostic accuracy, streamlining case retrieval, and improving patient care. The paper emphasizes that the resulting models remain insufficient for clinical deployment and require further robustness assessment, interpretability, regulatory compliance, and prospective validation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly identify biases inherent to a single-institution dataset. Data originate from one geographic and clinical setting, which may influence self-supervised training and limit generalizability to other populations. They suggest incorporating multiple institutions and more diverse patient populations to improve robustness.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset from one geographic and clinical setting, potentially limiting generalization to other populations. It covers non-contrast chest CT rather than other anatomical regions or imaging modalities. Variability in disease terminology across radiology reports can affect model detection accuracy. Comprehensive multi-abnormality segmentation and localization annotations remain planned future work. Models developed using the dataset are not ready for routine clinical deployment, and generated report quality remains insufficient for clinical use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training multimodal 3D medical-imaging foundation models through contrastive image-report pretraining; supervised multi-abnormality classification; fine-tuning; internal validation and benchmarking; zero-shot abnormality detection; volume-to-volume and report-to-volume retrieval; visual question answering; and radiology report generation. Anatomical segmentation labels support anatomical localization, visual grounding, and future fine-grained abnormality segmentation research. The dataset and associated code are publicly available for further research.
